title: Pointwise existence of normalized completed coefficient presentations
statement: For every scheme T, there exists a CoefficientPresentation l T E i identifying completed coefficients with native locally finite coefficients, under the same prime, field, algebra, finite-dimensionality, and NativeGeometry hypotheses.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Section 6.8; finite quotient realization and normalization at a fixed scheme

proof.text: Apply continuousCoefficientCompletion to E and T. It supplies the integral continuous-function sheaf as the limit of the positive constant residue tower, with each finite comparison fixed on constants and each projection given by pointwise reduction.

Identify the commutative residue tower, after forgetting commutativity, with integralCoefficientSheafSystem. The components are identity maps, and consecutive quotient maps agree. The forgetful functor on ring sheaves is fully faithful and preserves limits. Its preimage of the canonical limit isomorphism identifies finiteCoefficientLimit with completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted. The limit-isomorphism projection equations prove that this isomorphism preserves every recorded residue projection.
Use continuousCoefficientLocalization for the normalized localization isomorphism, and integralRationalCoefficientMap with its pointwise normalization for the integral inclusion.

Construct rational inclusion by sending s to the function x ↦ i(s(x)). The spectral norm makes E a normed Q_l-algebra, so the linear map i is continuous by finite dimensionality. Its image is a finite-dimensional Q_l-subspace; hence the composite is locally finite. The sheaf/presheaf monoidal comparison identities identify the native ring unit and multiplication with the pointwise ones. Pointwise operations then prove the ring-map equations, and precomposition proves naturality. This construction has the required pointwise normalization, including on the empty object. Assemble these data into CoefficientPresentation, transporting the completion residue equations using the projection-preserving isomorphism from step 2.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2) and Definition 6.8.1; reuse the existing normalized completion/localization theorems and explicitly construct finite-field postcomposition.
